articles.title: Scientists Discovered A New Cat Before Rockstar Could Finish GTA 6
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development since 2015, and a lot of things have happened since then, including the recent discovery a new species of cat. The scientific journal Current Biology disclosed the discovery of Leopardus tilcayo--known as the tilcayo tiger cat--this week.
body: The tilcayo tiger cat is the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years.

Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, a co-author of the report, told NBC News that it is currently unknown how many of the cats remain in the wild. She said she discovered the cat basically by accident. She volunteers at a wildlife rehab facility close to La Paz, Bolivia and noticed a tiny cat that she thought was a kitten.

The cat was brought to the facility by a man who was caring for it, feeding it rice and eggs, and later giving it up when he was unable to care for it. Genetic testing was undertaken, and it was discovered that it was indeed a brand-new species of cat never before discovered or documented.

As for more gaming-related things that have happened since GTA 5 came out, GameSpot recently assembled a collection of some of the biggest news stories, including Halo coming to PlayStation, the release of 15+ Call of Duty games, the entire run of Phil Spencer as Xbox CEO, and more.
points: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development since 2015, and a lot of things have happened since then, including the recent discovery a new species of cat.
The scientific journal Current Biology disclosed the discovery of Leopardus tilcayo--known as the tilcayo tiger cat--this week.

articles.title: Activision Calls Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 'The Epic Conclusion,' Leaving Fans Wondering What's Next
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is being advertised as the "epic conclusion," suggesting an end of an era for the franchise. In the social copy for the latest trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Activision stated that the game will be an "epic conclusion" for the Modern Warfare saga.
body: Although it's likely just a marketing buzz term, the branding comes at an interesting time. Earlier this week, Treyarch design director Kevin Drew stated that the studio was ready to "make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before." The comments come as the studio waved goodbye to two back-to-back Black Ops games, with the most recent one being regarded as an underwhelming misfire for the series. The comments led fans to speculate that the Black Ops series may be coming to an end, or at least taking a break, allowing Treyarch to make its first new subfranchise in nearly 20 years.

Some fans are already waving goodbye to the current Modern Warfare series. "Reboot it again," joked one fan in a post on the Call of Duty subreddit. "They should do a COD Ghosts 2 or Infinite Warfare 2, both underrated campaigns," suggested another who may or may not be joking.
points: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is being advertised as the "epic conclusion," suggesting an end of an era for the franchise.

The popcorn goes in the bucket, and then you can put it on your head and grab the popcorn from up there. Or you can plop it in your lap and eat the popcorn normally. In a word, the popcorn bucket is perfect. If you need three words, Rhodes said the popcorn bucket is "aerodynamic, ergonomic, delicious."
Check out the glorious announcement video for the Street Fighter popcorn bucket below.
Tickets for the Street Fighter movie go on sale this coming Monday, September, 21. Presumably that's also when people can reserve one of these popcorn buckets, so the price should be revealed soon.

The Street Fighter movie releases in theaters on October 16. In addition to Rhodes as Guile, the film features Noah Centineo as Ken, Andrew Koji as Ryu, Roman Reigns as Akuma, Jason Momoa as Blanka, 50 Cent as Balrog, David Dastmalchian as M. Bison, and Eric Andre as Don Sauvage.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Is Eager to Adapt His Books into a Video Game, Calling Himself a 'Lifelong Gamer'
articles.summary: During an exclusive interview with IGN, Brandon Sanderson has expressed interest in potentially adapting his Mistborn book series into a video game, but only if he can find the right studio to partner with.
body: "As a lifelong gamer, suffice it to say that yes, I've thought about this a lot.
"The key will be the right partner. Video games, even the smaller indie games, are huge investments these days.
"Mistborn would almost certainly be the first thing I would try, as the mechanics of the magic and world very naturally lend themselves to such an adaptation – but again, I'd need the right partner."
So it doesn't sound like we'll be getting a Mistborn game anytime soon, but it's certainly on the cards for the distant future after Sanderson's recent comments.

articles.title: Gears Of War: E-Day On PC Won’t Let You Play Without A Ray Tracing-Capable GPU
articles.summary: Ahead of its release next month, the official PC specs for Gears of War: E-Day have been revealed. The next game in the series has looked good in recent previews, and if you're aiming to reach a high level of fidelity, you're going to need some fairly chunky PC hardware for 4K gibs and perfect…
body: One thing worth pointing out is that graphics cards without dedicated ray-tracing hardware aren't supported. It's not the first time this has been the case--Indiana Jones and the Great Circle being a prime example--but it does create a hard generational lock for interested players. By making ray-tracing hardware a baseline requirement, the game completely phases out massively popular GPUs like the GTX 1060 or AMD's RX 5000 series, making the RTX 2060 the absolute minimum threshold for playing the new Gears of War.

Developer The Coalition says it has continued to iterate and improve PC stability and performance across a wide range of hardware configurations since July, and if you're aiming to run the game at 1080p and 60fps, you'll need a GPU like an Nvidia GeForce RTX 2060, an entry-level RTX 5050, or an AMD Radeon RX 6600 with 6GB of VRAM. Hitting the 1440p 60fps sweet spot increases the hardware requirements to GPUs with 8GB of VRAM, while running the game at 4K 60fps means you'll need a 12GB GeForce RTX 5070 Ti or an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT.

articles.title: New R-Rated Survival Sci-Fi Officially Crowned Highest-Rated Video Game Adaptation Ever
articles.summary: It's official: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil film is a hit with critics. The movie currently sits at a 96% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, making it the highest-rated video game movie on the site—it isn’t particularly close either.
body: After these first three entries, there are only six video game movies on the list with positive Tomatometer scores: The Angry Birds Movie 2, Sonic the Hedgehog 2, Pokémon Detective Pikachu, Gran Turismo, Sonic the Hedgehog, and Mortal Kombat II. Their scores range from 64% to 72%. This short list shows just how bad video game movies tend to be.

For clarity, the Tomatometer represents the percentage of critics who gave a movie a favorable review. This Rotten Tomatoes list excludes films that don’t have at least 20 reviews from theatrical releases. That said, the Rotten Tomatoes list consists of just a handful of movies. For instance, Exit 8, an adaptation of the game of the same name, has a 91% Rotten Tomatoes score with 176 reviews. Even so, Resident Evil is well ahead of the competition.

Until now, video game adaptations have fared dramatically better on the small screen than in theaters, with great TV shows like Cyberpunk: Edgerunners (100% on Rotten Tomatoes), Arcane (100%), Fallout (93%), The Last of Us (96%), Castlevania (94%), Nier: Automata Ver1.1a, and more.

articles.title: Doctor Who Reboot Shows First Signs of Life in New BBC Update
articles.summary: Like the sci-fi show's titular Time Lord, Doctor Who is starting to regenerate. Following the series' effective cancellation earlier this year, the BBC is now searching for a new production team for a reboot.
body: The BBC published official documentation today announcing that it has begun a "tendering" process in which it will take pitches from production companies to pick up the franchise. The timeline is moving pretty quickly, as the deadline for submissions is Oct. 1. That's only two weeks away, so if you happen to have a lot of money and run a production company, you better get on it. After submissions close, the BBC plans to conduct interviews with potential candidates by the end of January next year, with a final decision expected to be made in March. If all goes according to plan, the newest iteration of Doctor Who will premiere in 2028 or 2029.

articles.title: Valor Mortis is only $40 because its developer knows you'll be choosing from a lot of big games over this "stacked" autumn
articles.summary: The Valor Mortis developer has announced the game's price and offered an explanation as to why the team picked this particular price point. Valor Mortis costs $40 / €40, which is notably cheaper than other games releasing around the same time. We've asked for clarification on UK price.
body: The developer posted a message on X explaining its decision, saying that while it's confident in the game, it understands that players' time and money are at a premium in this period.

"We have had many discussions over the past year about the price of Valor Mortis. We believe the game has the quality, fidelity, and playtime in its 20-hour story to go toe-to-toe with many 'full price' titles," the developer wrote. "Still, this fall is stacked and there's high demand for your time and money."

Valor Mortis is the ambitious first-person Soulslike from Ghostrunner developer One More Level. It launches 13th October, notably in close proximity to Gears of War: E-Day, Ace Combat 8, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Final Fantasy Resonance, and Phantom Blade Zero in October alone. It's also within striking distance of several big September releases such as Marvel's Wolverine, Silent Hill: Townfall, and Control Resonant - which you may recall is the game that caused Valor Mortis to be pushed back to October from its original 24th September release date.

articles.summary: Have you ever waded through a week of rapid-fire video game news and felt an immediate need to unpack it immediately, lest your head explode? That’s sure how we felt after trying to figure out if we’d be alive long enough to play Starcraft.
body: This past weekend, Blizzard hosted its annual Blizzcon event. It was a particularly loaded one, complete with surprise reveals that laid out the studio’s next four years. Well, theoretically at least. There’s the whole “heat death of the universe thing” that could get in Diablo 5 ’s way. Still, Blizzcon pointed out a lot of things that beg for discussion on Point It Out!, our weekly news series that’s built for moments like this. We love when people point at things. We love pointing at things. It’s a match made in heaven.

This week Simone de Rochefort is joined by a very special guest to help break it down: me, Polygon Editor-At-Large Giovanni Colantonio. I filled in for Editor-In-Chief Matt Patches, who has temporarily been exiled to France after committing sock-related crimes on last week’s episode. He will return once he has learned how to crack the perfect apology to our perturbed audience. Until then, the Italians will have their moment in the sun.
